'''''Malva trimestris''''' (synonyms ''Althaea trimestris'', ''Lavatera trimestris''), [[common name]]s '''annual mallow''', '''rose mallow''', '''royal mallow''', '''regal mallow''',<ref>[http://www.malvaceae.info/Genera/Lavatera/annual.html#trimestris ''L. trimestris'' at Malvaceae Info]</ref> and '''common annual tree mallow'''<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/119872/i-Lavatera-trimestris-i/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Lavatera trimestris'' | access-date = 20 March 2018}}</ref><ref>[http://www.malvaceae.info/Synonymy/Synonymy.php?file=Lavatera Synonymy of ''Lavatera'' at Malvaceae Info]</ref> is a species of flowering plant [[native plant|native]] to the Mediterranean region.

It is an [[annual plant|annual]] growing to {{cvt|120|cm|0}} tall by {{cvt|45|cm|0}} wide, producing shallow funnel-shaped flowers in summer, in shades of white and pink, with maroon centres and maroon veining on the petals.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> The Latin ''trimestris'' literally means "of three months", referring to the growing and flowering period.<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref> 

This plant is widely cultivated, often under the name ''Lavatera trimestris''. Numerous [[cultivars]] have been developed for garden use, all of which are annuals to be sown in spring for flowering the same year. The cultivars 'Beauty Series' <ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/176788/Lavatera-trimestris-Beauty-Series/Details | title = ''Lavatera trimesttris'' Beauty Series | publisher = RHS | access-date = 1 October 2020}}</ref> and 'Silver Cup'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Lavatera trimestris'' 'Silver Cup'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/119256/Lavatera-trimestris-Silver-Cup/Details | access-date = 2 October 2020}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 59 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 20 March 2018}}</ref>
